headline: AMEX DRILLS 227 g/t Au OVER 0.50m AT PERRON — Resource Conversion Opens Denise Zone Extension to the East (TSXV:AMX)
snippet: Amex Exploration (TSXV: AMX) reported a resource-conversion hole at its Perron Gold Project in Quebec grading 227.46 g/t Au over 0.50 m (hole PE-26-959) while simultaneously expanding the Denise Zone approximately 320 m eastward via new exploration drilling. The high-grade hit continues Perron's track record as one of Quebec's most prolific undeveloped gold systems; results are part of the 2026 resource expansion program targeting a maiden resource update.

headline: FREEGOLD VENTURES HITS 160.6m AT 1.80 g/t Au AT GOLDEN SUMMIT — 50,000m Campaign Intact, 2027 Alaska PFS On Track (TSX:FVL)
snippet: Freegold Ventures (TSX: FVL) released new assays from its 50,000-metre 2026 drill campaign at Golden Summit in Alaska, headlined by 160.6 m at 1.80 g/t Au from 578.2 m depth at the Cleary zone. With over 50 holes still pending assay and drilling running through early December, the company confirmed it remains on track for an updated resource estimate and a 2027 prefeasibility study — moving a bulk-tonnage gold system toward a construction decision.

headline: NORTHERN STAR CEO OPENS DOOR TO GOLD FIELDS TALKS — $38.7B Hostile Bid Enters New Phase as Vadnagra Signals Openness to Improved Offer
snippet: Northern Star Resources' new CEO Suresh Vadnagra told the Australian Financial Review that the board is open to discussions with Gold Fields if the South African miner improves its A$38.7 billion (US$27.1 billion) unsolicited offer. Gold Fields is simultaneously weighing a sale of its ~A$1.1 billion stake in Northern Star to fund a cash-heavier revised bid, according to Bloomberg, with an Australian investor roadshow wrapping up in late October. A deal would create one of the five largest gold miners on Earth.

headline: LITHIUM CARBONATE FUTURES SLIDE TO 2026 LOWS BELOW CNY 90,000/t — Persistent Oversupply Deepens as Producers Hold Output Schedules
snippet: Lithium carbonate futures fell below the CNY 90,000 per tonne threshold on October 29, marking fresh 2026 lows according to SP Angel's morning market view. The slide reflects persistent oversupply after CATL returned the Jianxiawo mine to care and maintenance while producers like Liontown maintained output schedules despite falling prices. The CNY 90,000 level is widely watched as a cash-cost floor for Chinese lepidolite producers — a break below it historically triggers production curtailments.

headline: GOLD HITS THREE-MONTH LOW AT $3,994, SILVER LOSES $54 SUPPORT — December Fed Hike Now Priced at Over 80%
snippet: ISA Bullion's October 26 daily metals analysis flagged gold touching a three-month low at $3,994 as the metal attempted to snap a two-day losing streak, while silver confirmed a technical breakdown below the key $54 support level. Markets were pricing in over 80% probability of a Federal Reserve rate hike at the December meeting following Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish commentary, compounding selling pressure on non-yielding assets. Gold has now retraced approximately 25% from its January 2026 all-time high above $5,300.

headline: RECORD CENTRAL BANK BUYING ISN'T LIFTING MINING STOCKS — Equities Fall 2–5× Harder Than Gold Despite 289t Q2 Record
snippet: Discovery Alert's October analysis finds gold mining equities are falling two to five times harder than spot gold in 2026, despite a record 289 tonnes of central bank buying in Q2 — the highest Q2 total in history. The piece identifies elevated all-in sustaining costs, currency headwinds in producer countries, and a breakdown in the traditional gold price-to-earnings leverage ratio as the structural causes. Junior miners, with no production to protect margins, are absorbing the full force of the repricing.

headline: GLOBAL ENERGY METALS IDENTIFIES MULTIPLE URANIUM TARGETS AT CHARLOT-NEELY LAKE — 20km North of Uranium City in Athabasca Basin (TSXV:GEMC)
snippet: Global Energy Metals (TSXV: GEMC) highlighted identification of multiple uranium targets at its royalty-held Charlot-Neely Lake project, approximately 20 km north of Uranium City on the northwestern margin of Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin. The targets follow airborne radiometric survey work identifying prominent anomalies across Terra North Resources' 594 km² Saskatchewan uranium portfolio. With uranium long-term contract prices topping the 2007 record at $96.50/lb, Athabasca Basin project-generation activity is running at its highest pace in over a decade.

headline: LME COPPER STOCKPILES RISE 4.91% TO 245,275t — Analysts Split on Whether Inventory Build Signals Price Correction Ahead
snippet: LME-registered copper stockpiles rose 4.91% to 245,275 tonnes in the latest reading, raising questions about whether the metal's near-record price above $14,000/t is sustainable. Discovery Alert's October analysis notes that stockpiles are still down roughly 42% year-to-date and the Yangshan import premium near 13-year highs suggests genuine Chinese physical demand — but any sustained inventory build at current LME levels typically precedes a $500–$1,000/t correction. Copper-focused explorers like FireFly Metals and Surge Copper are closely watched for price-sensitivity signals.

headline: GHANA REVIEWS GOLD FIELDS' MINE LICENSE — Government Weighs Domestic Control of Key Asset, Adding Sovereign Risk to Hostile Bid Saga
snippet: Ghana's government is evaluating whether domestic companies should assume control of major foreign-held mining operations, with Gold Fields' license renewal for a key Ghanaian asset reportedly under review, according to Bloomberg as cited in Frank Holmes' October 26 Gold SWOT column. The development adds meaningful sovereign risk to Gold Fields at precisely the moment the company is stretching its balance sheet to pursue its A$38.7 billion hostile bid for Northern Star. West African regulatory pressure on foreign miners has intensified in 2026 following similar moves in Mali, Guinea, and Burkina Faso.

headline: PALADIN ENERGY POSTS RECORD LANGER HEINRICH QUARTER — 2.1Mlb U3O8 Produced, Most Since 2023 Restart (ASX:PDN)
snippet: Paladin Energy (ASX: PDN) reported record uranium production of 2.1 million pounds U3O8 at its Langer Heinrich mine in Namibia for the September 2026 quarter — its strongest output since the mine was restarted in 2023 after a decade on care and maintenance. The result was cited in SP Angel's October 29 morning market view as evidence that tier-one uranium restart projects are now de-risked, a positive read-through for other advanced restart candidates across the Athabasca Basin and Kazakhstan.
